name: Onasemnogene abeparvovec
summary: An AAV9 gene therapy for spinal muscular atrophy. A non-replicating viral capsid carries a working copy of the gene for SMN protein into motor neurons, where it is expressed without integrating into the chromosomes.

target.name: SMN gene replacement in motor neurons

journey.title: Infused into a vein
journey.text: Given once as an intravenous infusion.

journey.title: Carried in the blood
journey.text: The AAV9 capsid can cross the blood–brain barrier, which lets an intravenous dose reach neurons in the spinal cord.

journey.title: Reaches motor neurons
journey.text: In spinal muscular atrophy, motor neurons in the spinal cord lack enough SMN protein because SMN1 is lost or mutated.

journey.title: Also reaches the liver
journey.text: AAV9 also transduces the liver. Acute serious liver injury and acute liver failure carry a boxed warning, so liver function is monitored.

journey.title: Vector DNA is shed
journey.text: Vector DNA is shed for a time in saliva, urine and stool.

mechanism.title: The capsid attaches
mechanism.text: The AAV9 capsid binds the cell surface and is taken up by endocytosis.

mechanism.title: It travels to the nucleus
mechanism.text: The capsid escapes the endosome and moves toward the nucleus.

mechanism.title: The gene is delivered
mechanism.text: In the nucleus the capsid releases its self-complementary DNA, which persists mostly as a separate episome rather than integrating into the chromosomes.

mechanism.title: SMN protein is made
mechanism.text: The SMN transgene, driven by a CMV enhancer / chicken-β-actin hybrid promoter, is transcribed and translated into SMN protein.

facts.label: Genome
facts.value: Self-complementary DNA carrying human SMN cDNA

facts.label: Fate in the nucleus
facts.value: Persists mostly as a non-integrated episome

facts.label: Boxed warning
facts.value: Acute serious liver injury and acute liver failure

simplified: Receptor binding, endosomal escape and nuclear entry are each shown as one step. AAV entry involves several receptors and trafficking routes.
Uncoating is shown at the nucleus; where AAV capsids actually uncoat is still being studied.
The body map is a schematic. The spinal cord is drawn on the midline, in front of the organs, for visibility.
